## Purpose and status

This is an internal `fplida` explainer for the Census of Population and
Housing products. It records the intended row units, current synthetic output,
official ABS variable meanings, and code labels that should be used when the
Census generator is rebuilt for dictionary accuracy.

This note is stricter than a descriptive package vignette. The current
generator emits several compact or approximate code systems under official
2021 Census mnemonics. Those approximations are useful synthetic placeholders,
but they are not sufficient if the package is meant to mimic the Census
Dictionary. The rebuild should treat the ABS 2021 Census Dictionary as the
primary source of truth for variable scope, category labels, supplementary
codes, and numeric ranges.

An earlier high-priority gap was `HSCP`, Highest year of school completed. The
current generated schema now emits `HSCP`, and local tests constrain it to the
ABS-style code set. The remaining Census problem is broader: every generated
ABS mnemonic needs a durable source link or frozen code table, and generated
category frequencies remain local implementation evidence unless an official
distribution source is attached.

## Source documents

The interpretation in this note is based on these source classes.

1. Primary ABS Census Dictionary sources:

   - [ABS 2021 Census Dictionary: Variables index](https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-index)
   - [ABS 2021 Census Dictionary: Highest year of school completed (HSCP)](https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/education-and-training/highest-year-school-completed-hscp)
   - [ABS Understanding supplementary codes in Census variables](https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/detailed-methodology-information/information-papers/understanding-supplementary-codes-census-variables)

   The variables index is the primary source for the list of 2021 Census
   variables and official variable pages. Individual variable pages define
   scope, categories, not-applicable populations, derivation notes, and data-use
   considerations.

2. Local PLIDA metadata:

   - `inst/plida_metadata/datasets.csv`
   - `inst/plida_metadata/products.csv`
   - `inst/plida_metadata/variables.csv`
   - `data-raw/PLIDA data item list - 19MAR2026.xlsx`

   These files define the PLIDA product names and local Census variable
   inventory for 2011, 2016, and 2021 Census products.

3. Local generator and foundation files:

   - `R/generate_census.R`
   - `src/rust/src/census_2021.rs`
   - `inst/foundations/census_2021.toml`

   These define the current synthetic schema, current code values, and
   distributional approximations.

The rebuild should use the ABS pages directly, not the current generator
constants, when deciding what numeric or supplementary code values mean.

## Source-backed coverage decisions

| Product area | What the research source supports | What is still not found |
|---|---|---|
| Census variable definitions and code labels | The ABS 2021 Census Dictionary is the official source for variable definition, scope, categories, derivation, form questions, history, and data-use considerations. It should override local generator constants whenever a column uses an ABS mnemonic. The Census code-evidence register now attaches ABS Dictionary URLs for generated mnemonics where a public page exists. | The rebuild still needs frozen machine-readable code tables for large classifications and any future dictionary-accuracy tests that go beyond URL-level evidence. |
| Supplementary codes | The ABS supplementary-codes paper supports the use of symbol codes such as `&`, `@`, and `V` and explains that code width varies by variable. | PLIDA-specific geography fields such as `STEUCP` and `STEUCD` still need DIL/ASGS verification because they are not exposed as ordinary public Census Dictionary pages in the same way as standard Census mnemonics. |
| Current generator distributions | Local foundation files and current generator output support implementation checks only. | I did not find an official source that validates the current generated category frequencies or foundation distribution weights. |

## Product structure

`generate_census()` writes three 2021 Census products under `abs-census/`.

| Product | Current file stem | Row unit | Current source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Person | `madipge-cen21-d-person-2021` | One row per synthetic person. | Projected from the synthetic spine. |
| Family | `madipge-cen21-d-family-2021` | One row per generated family. | Generated independently in Rust. |
| Dwelling | `madipge-cen21-d-dwelling-2021` | One row per generated dwelling. | Generated independently in Rust. |

The person table is then assigned `DWELLING_ID` and `FAMILY_ID` values by
sampling from generated dwelling and family tables. This gives linkable
synthetic tables, but it does not currently enforce all household composition,
relationship, age, family, and dwelling consistency constraints that the real
Census products imply.

The local PLIDA metadata also contains 2011 and 2016 Census person, family, and
dwelling products. The current generator only builds the 2021 products.

## Variable-level schema register

Every generated variable observed in this pass for this guide is listed in
[`schema-registers/schema-register-census.csv`](schema-registers/schema-register-census.csv).
The register records R type, sampled generated missingness, sampled generated
domains/distributions, and direct PLIDA metadata matches. Treat those sampled
domains/distributions as implementation evidence only, not as official Census
data.

A rendered variable evidence appendix for this guide is available at [`variable-evidence-appendices/census-variable-evidence.qmd`](variable-evidence-appendices/census-variable-evidence.qmd). It contains one row per generated variable with observed generated values or distributions, local metadata/crosswalk status, and unresolved-source caveats.

A Census-specific code evidence register is available at [`census-variable-code-evidence.csv`](census-variable-code-evidence.csv), with a rendered companion note at [`census-variable-code-evidence.qmd`](census-variable-code-evidence.qmd). It maps all 57 generated Census variables to ABS Dictionary URLs where available, local DIL/identifier evidence where no public dictionary page was found, and the current generated-code assessment.

| Dataset | Generated variable rows | Direct PLIDA metadata matches | No direct PLIDA name match |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `CENSUS` | 57 | 57 | 0 |

The direct matches mean the current compact columns align by name with local
PLIDA metadata. Code labels still need to be checked against the ABS 2021
Census Dictionary and variables index before they are treated as official
source-data categories.

## Supplementary codes

ABS supplementary codes are not arbitrary missing-value numbers. The ABS
information paper explains that supplementary categories include:

- Not stated;
- Not applicable;
- Overseas visitor;
- Inadequately described;
- So described;
- Not further defined;
- Not elsewhere classified.

For many 2021 variables, these are represented with symbols rather than
ordinary numeric values. Examples include `&`, `&&`, `&&&`, and `&&&&` for not
stated; `@`, `@@`, `@@@`, and `@@@@` for not applicable; and `V`, `VV`, `VVV`,
and `VVVV` for overseas visitors. The number of repeated symbols depends on
the variable's code width.

Important implications for the rebuild:

- Do not use `0` as a generic not-applicable code unless the ABS page says so.
- Do not use `9`, `99`, or `999` as a generic not-stated code unless the ABS
  page says so for that variable.
- Preserve leading zeroes for variables such as `INCP`, `HRWRP`, `MTWP`, `HRSP`,
  `RNTD`, and `MRED`.
- Store code variables as character if the code set mixes digits and
  supplementary symbols.

## Rebuild priorities

The current generator has moved many earlier mismatches to ABS-style code
sets. The remaining work is to freeze official code tables for every generated
ABS mnemonic, keep local identifiers separate, and stop treating generated
frequencies as official Census distributions.

| Variable/family | Current status | Required next step |
|---|---|---|
| Small categorical code sets | Current tests constrain `HSCP`, `INGP`, `CITP`, `MSTP`, `INCP`, `LFSP`, `HRWRP`, long-term health indicators, unpaid-work/care variables, `ADFP`, `STUP`, `STRD`, `TEND`, `BEDRD`, `VEHRD`, `NPRD`, and `SSCF` to ABS-style code domains. | Keep validating against the official ABS pages, and keep generated frequencies labelled local. |
| Large classifications | `BPLP`, `LANP`, `RELP`, `HEAP`, `OCCP`, `INDP`, `MTWP`, and `FMCF` have official ABS Dictionary pages, but the generator emits subsets, top-level codes, or compact classifications. | Add frozen full code tables or explicitly rename any deliberately collapsed variables. |
| Dollar-code variables | `RNTD` and `MRED` are emitted as character dollar-code fields with supplementary codes, and tests constrain `MRED` to `0000`-`9999`. | Keep them as character codes; do not treat generated dollar values as official rent or mortgage distributions. |
| Local identifiers and DIL-only fields | `SYNTHETIC_AEUID`, `DWELLING_ID`, and `FAMILY_ID` are package linkage keys. `DOBYP`, `STEUCP`, and `STEUCD` are local PLIDA/DIL or ASGS-style evidence rather than public Census Dictionary pages. | Keep these out of ABS code-label claims unless DIL/ASGS sources are attached. |

### Education

#### Highest year of school completed (HSCP)

ABS defines `HSCP` as the highest level of primary or secondary schooling
completed. Scope is persons aged 15 years and over. The not-applicable (`@`)
category comprises persons aged under 15 years. The ABS form instruction says
people currently at school should select the highest year they have completed,
not the year they are currently undertaking.

| Code | Correct ABS category |
|---|---|
| `1` | Year 12 or equivalent |
| `2` | Year 11 or equivalent |
| `3` | Year 10 or equivalent |
| `4` | Year 9 or equivalent |
| `5` | Year 8 or below |
| `6` | Did not go to school |
| `&` | Not stated |
| `@` | Not applicable |
| `V` | Overseas visitor |

Current `fplida` treatment: `HSCP` is emitted and tested against the ABS-style
code set, but generated frequencies are local.

#### Level of highest educational attainment (HEAP)

`HEAP` is a hierarchical ABS education variable. The current generator uses a
compact integer system that is not the full ABS HEAP code system. At the
highest hierarchy level, ABS uses:

| Code | Correct ABS top-level category |
|---|---|
| `1` | Postgraduate Degree Level |
| `2` | Graduate Diploma and Graduate Certificate Level |
| `3` | Bachelor Degree Level |
| `4` | Advanced Diploma and Diploma Level |
| `5` | Certificate III & IV Level |
| `6` | Secondary Education - Years 10 and above |
| `7` | Certificate I & II Level |
| `8` | Secondary Education - Years 9 and below |
| `9` | Supplementary Codes |
| `&`, `&&`, `&&&` | Not stated at different hierarchy depths |
| `@`, `@@`, `@@@` | Not applicable at different hierarchy depths |
| `V`, `VV`, `VVV` | Overseas visitor at different hierarchy depths |

The full HEAP page contains two- and three-character child codes such as `611 =
Year 12`, `613 = Year 11`, `621 = Year 10`, `811 = Year 9`, and `812 = Year 8
or below`. The rebuild should decide which HEAP level to emit and then preserve
the matching code width and supplementary-code width.

#### Student status (STUP)

| Code | Correct ABS category |
|---|---|
| `1` | Not attending |
| `2` | Full-time student |
| `3` | Part-time student |
| `4` | Institution (`TYPP`) stated, full-time/part-time status (`STUP`) not stated |
| `&` | Both not stated |
| `V` | Overseas visitor |

Current `fplida` treatment uses the ABS-style code order in local tests.

| `08` | $650-$799 ($33,800-$41,599) |
| `09` | $800-$999 ($41,600-$51,999) |
| `10` | $1,000-$1,249 ($52,000-$64,999) |

#### Hours worked

`HRSP` records hours worked as `00` to `99` hours singly, plus `&&`, `@@`, and
`VV`. `HRWRP` records ranges:

| Code | Correct ABS category |
|---|---|
| `00` | 0 hours |
| `01` | 1-9 hours |
| `02` | 10-19 hours |
| `03` | 20-29 hours |
| `04` | 30-34 hours |
| `05` | 35-39 hours |
| `06` | 40-44 hours |
| `07` | 45-49 hours |
| `08` | 50-59 hours |
| `09` | 60-69 hours |
| `10` | 70 hours or more |
| `&&` | Not stated |
| `@@` | Not applicable |
| `VV` | Overseas visitor |

The current generator uses the ABS-style range code set in local tests. Its
hours distribution remains a synthetic local distribution.

#### Occupation, industry, and method of travel to work

`OCCP`, `INDP`, and `MTWP` are large classification variables. The current
generator now uses official-width Census codes where the spine supports them:

- `OCCP` is emitted at the 6-digit ANZSCO occupation level for employed people
  aged 15 years and over. A calibrated share of otherwise-valid occupations is
  reported as the matching major group's 6-digit `nfd` code, with a higher
  `nfd` rate for Managers than other major groups. Spine occupation codes that
  are not in the `strayr::anzsco2019` occupation list are also remapped to the
  matching major-group `nfd` code; people outside scope use `@@@@@@`.
- `INDP` uses a small set of industry codes from the spine or a sampled set.
- `MTWP` uses a compact `1` to `11` scheme.

The ABS pages for these variables contain much larger official code tables.
For example, `MTWP` includes detailed single-mode and multimode combinations
with codes such as `001 = Train`, `002 = Bus`, and many multimode combinations.
The rebuild should source these code tables directly from the ABS variable
pages and decide whether to emit full detail or a deliberately renamed
collapsed variable. If the column is called `MTWP`, it should use ABS `MTWP`
codes.

## Health variables

The 2021 Census introduced selected long-term health condition variables. The
current generator emits a condition count and separate condition indicators,
but the separate indicators use `1` and `0`. ABS condition variables use
condition-specific three-character codes.

### Count of selected long-term health conditions (CLTHP)

| Code | Correct ABS category |
|---|---|
| `0` | None of the selected conditions |
| `1` | One condition |
| `2` | Two conditions |
| `3` | Three or more conditions |
| `&` | Not stated |
| `V` | Overseas visitor |

### Specific condition variables

| Variable | Has condition | Does not have condition | Not stated | Overseas visitor |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `HARTP` | `011` Has arthritis | `012` Does not have arthritis | `&&&` | `VVV` |
| `HASTP` | `021` Has asthma | `022` Does not have asthma | `&&&` | `VVV` |
| `HCANP` | `031` Has cancer (including remission) | `032` Does not have cancer (including remission) | `&&&` | `VVV` |
| `HDEMP` | `041` Has dementia (including Alzheimer's) | `042` Does not have dementia (including Alzheimer's) | `&&&` | `VVV` |
| `HDIAP` | `051` Has diabetes (excluding gestational diabetes) | `052` Does not have diabetes (excluding gestational diabetes) | `&&&` | `VVV` |
| `HHEDP` | `061` Has heart disease (including heart attack or angina) | `062` Does not have heart disease (including heart attack or angina) | `&&&` | `VVV` |
| `HKIDP` | `071` Has kidney disease | `072` Does not have kidney disease | `&&&` | `VVV` |
| `HLUNP` | `081` Has a lung condition (including COPD or emphysema) | `082` Does not have a lung condition (including COPD or emphysema) | `&&&` | `VVV` |
| `HMHCP` | `091` Has a mental health condition (including depression or anxiety) | `092` Does not have a mental health condition (including depression or anxiety) | `&&&` | `VVV` |
| `HSTRP` | `101` Has had a stroke | `102` Has not had a stroke | `&&&` | `VVV` |

The current generator does not emit `HOLHP` for other long-term condition(s) or
`HLTHP` for whether a person has one or more long-term conditions. If those are
added, use the ABS pages for their exact codes.

| `MRED` | Monthly mortgage repayments: `0000` to `9999` singly; `&&&& = Not stated`; `@@@@ = Not applicable`. | Values are not ranges. Maximum valid numeric code is `9999`. | Current tests require four-character dollar/supplementary codes and constrain numeric values to `9999` or below; amounts are synthetic. |
| `STEUCD` | State of dwelling/enumeration geography in local PLIDA metadata. | Verify against PLIDA DIL and ASGS conventions. | Generated from state weights independently of person state. |

## Family variables

| Variable | Correct ABS values | Current fplida status |
|---|---|---|
| `FAMILY_ID` | Synthetic family identifier. | Identifier, not a Census Dictionary category. |
| `FMCF` | Top-level ABS labels include `1 = Couple family with no children`, `2 = Couple family with children`, `3 = One parent family`, `9 = Other family`, and `@@@@ = Not applicable`; lower hierarchy levels are available on the ABS page. | Current generator emits top-level ABS-style family composition codes; full hierarchical detail still needs a frozen official code table if implemented. |
| `CDCF` | Count of dependent children in family. | Current tests require Census-style two-character count/supplementary codes; verify exact full category semantics before expanding detail. |
| `CPRF` | Count of persons in family. | Current tests require values within the compact count domain; generated distribution is local. |
| `SSCF` | `1 = Male same-sex couple`; `2 = Female same-sex couple`; `3 = Opposite-sex couple`; `@ = Not applicable`. | Current generator uses this ABS-style code set. |

## Numeric and range variables

The rebuild should distinguish between true numeric values, range-coded
categories, and dollar-value code fields.

| Variable | Correct interpretation |
|---|---|
| `AGEP` | Single-year age. |
| `DOBYP` | Year of birth in current package; verify against DIL if retained. |
| `HRSP` | Hours worked, `00` to `99` singly, with `&&`, `@@`, `VV`. Use character codes. |
| `RNTD` | Weekly rent, `0001` to `9999` singly, with `&&&&`, `@@@@`. Use character codes. |
| `MRED` | Monthly mortgage repayments, `0000` to `9999` singly, with `&&&&`, `@@@@`. Use character codes. |
| `INCP` | Income range code, not a dollar amount. Top-coded at `$3,500 or more` per week. |
| `AGE5P`, `AGE10P`, `HRWRP`, `BEDRD`, `VEHRD`, `NPRD` | Range-coded categories, not continuous numeric values. |

## Missingness and not applicable

For current `fplida` output, `NA` often means the generator did not create a
value. For dictionary-accurate Census output, many missingness states should be
encoded with ABS supplementary codes instead.

Examples:

- `HSCP @` means not applicable, with the ABS page specifying persons aged
  under 15 years.
- `INCP @@` means not applicable for a two-character income code.
- Health-condition variables use `&&&` for not stated and `VVV` for overseas
  visitor.
- `RNTD` and `MRED` use four-character supplementary codes because their dollar
  values are four-character codes.

The rebuild should therefore avoid integer-only storage for variables whose
official code set includes supplementary symbols or leading zeroes.

## Validation checks for rebuild

Required shape checks:

- Person, family, and dwelling products use the product names in
  `inst/plida_metadata/products.csv`.
- Generated columns match the intended 2021 Census schema.
- `HSCP` is present if the generator claims to cover school-completion
  variables.
- Every official mnemonic column uses the exact ABS code set for that mnemonic,
  or the variable is renamed as a package-specific collapsed variable.

Required label checks:

- `HSCP` has exactly `1`, `2`, `3`, `4`, `5`, `6`, `&`, `@`, `V`.
- `INCP` preserves `01` to `09` leading zeroes and the top-coded `16` category.
- `HRWRP` uses `00` for 0 hours and `10` for 70 hours or more.
- Health indicators use condition-specific codes, not Boolean `0`/`1`.
- `MSTP`, `STUP`, `VOLWP`, `UNCAREP`, `DOMP`, `ADFP`, `TEND`, `FMCF`, and
  `SSCF` are checked against their ABS page labels.

Required consistency checks:

- Persons aged under 15 receive not-applicable codes for variables whose ABS
  scope excludes them, rather than `0`.
- Employment variables are only substantive for in-scope populations.
- Dwelling rent is only substantive for rented dwellings once `TEND` is recoded
  to ABS labels.
- Mortgage repayment is only substantive for mortgage dwellings once `TEND` is
  recoded to ABS labels.
- `DWELLING_ID` and `FAMILY_ID` assignments are consistent with generated
  family and dwelling counts.

## Promotion path

If this note becomes user-facing, the least disruptive path is:

1. Move or copy this file to `vignettes/census-dataset-explainer.qmd`.
2. Add executable validation chunks only after the generator uses ABS code
   systems.
3. Keep the official source links in this document but move the full machine
   readable label tables into a package data object or data-raw script.
4. Add tests that scrape or read frozen ABS code tables and compare every
   generated code against the expected code set.
